author: reek
body: THE SUPERBLOCK IS READ TWICE, BEFORE AND AFTER A WRITE, and the pair is the reading that matters. Before, there is no store in the partition and the inspector must say so; after, the same command at the same base must find one. An inspector that always answered "no superblock" would pass a test that only ran the first half, and an inspector that always answered with a superblock would pass one that only ran the second.

author: reek
body: WHAT THIS PAIR DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than left to be assumed: a difference at a NON-ZERO offset. Sectors 0 and 1 differ in their first byte, so `cmp-differ` exercises detection and the buffer property but not the reported offset. Arranging a late difference would mean writing a sector to set one up, which is a heavier fixture than the reading is worth while `cmp-same` already pins the traversal.

author: reek
body: A joined line rather than one print per element: the inspector answers lists, and a test that printed them element by element would need an effectful loop with an empty branch, which is more machinery than the reading is worth.
